questions.question: What is the core idea behind an n-gram language model?
options: Predicting the next word based on the counts of the previous n-1 words.
Using a neural network to predict the next character.
Translating a sentence into n different languages.
Counting how many times a word appears in the entire document.
questions.explanation: N-gram models are probabilistic and rely on the frequency of word sequences (n-grams) in a training corpus to estimate the likelihood of the next word.

questions.question: What is the 'zero-count problem' in n-gram models?
options: Any sequence of words not seen in training gets zero probability, making the whole sentence probability zero.
The model cannot count higher than zero.
The model ignores words that appear zero times in the dictionary.
The model's loss function starts at zero.
questions.explanation: Because language is so vast, most word sequences will never appear in a training set. Without smoothing, these unseen sequences break the model by assigning them zero probability.

questions.question: How does Kneser-Ney smoothing improve over simpler methods like Laplace?
options: It uses 'continuation probability' (how many contexts a word appears in) for the lower-order model.
It simply adds a larger number than 1 to every count.
It removes all rare words from the vocabulary.
It uses a transformer to predict the unseen n-grams.
questions.explanation: Kneser-Ney is clever: it realizes that a word like 'Francisco' appears frequently but only in one context ('San Francisco'), so it should have a low probability in other contexts.

questions.question: What does a perplexity of 100 on a held-out test set mean?
options: The model is as 'confused' as if it were choosing uniformly from 100 possible words at each step.
The model made 100 mistakes in total.
The model took 100 seconds to generate the text.
questions.explanation: Perplexity is a measure of uncertainty. A lower perplexity means the model is more certain about its predictions; 100 means the model narrows down the choices to about 100 words on average.
